test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 25 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: I walk at a speed of 10 km/h and reach the destination in 2 hrs. If I increase my speed by 5 km/h, how early would I reach my destination?
solution:
**Given:**

Initial Speed = 10 km/h

Time taken at initial speed = 2 hrs

Increased Speed = 10 km/h + 5 km/h = 15 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

Time Difference = Initial Time - New Time

**Calculation:**

Distance travelled = Initial Speed × Initial Time

⇒ Distance = 10 km/h × 2 hrs

⇒ Distance = 20 km

New Time = Distance / Increased Speed

⇒ New Time = 20 km / 15 km/h

⇒ New Time = (20)/(15) hrs

⇒ New Time = 4/3 hrs

⇒ New Time = 1 hr 20 min

Time Difference = Initial Time - New Time

⇒ Time Difference = 2 hrs - 1 hr 20 min

⇒ Time Difference = 40 min

**The correct answer is option 1 (40 min).**
